#+TITLE: Core Environment Layer
#+CATEGORY: core
#+PROPERTY: header-args:emacs-lisp :tangle yes

* Description
Synchronizes environment variables (especially ~$PATH~ and ~exec-path~) from the
user's login shell into graphical Emacs sessions. Also registers local tooling
directories (such as ~nodejs_tools~) so language servers and CLI formatters are
discovered seamlessly. Finally, it handles platform-specific OS modifier
pass-through settings and configures other utilities.

* Emacs Configuration
** Environment & Path Synchronization
Graphical Emacs often boots without inheriting environment variables defined in
shell configurations (~.bashrc~, ~.zshrc~). Using ~exec-path-from-shell~
guarantees that tools installed via Homebrew, NVM, or SDKMAN! are visible to
Emacs.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(use-package exec-path-from-shell
  :ensure t ; Make sure it works even when "use-package-always-ensure" is not yet configured
  :config
  ;; 1. Disable the interactive flag (-i) to prevent shell hanging on Linux
  (setq exec-path-from-shell-arguments '("-l"))

  ;; 2. Synchronize environment variables in GUI frames
  (when (memq window-system '(mac ns x pgtk))
    (exec-path-from-shell-initialize)))
#+end_src

** Local Tooling Execution Paths
In addition to system PATH inheritance, we prepend our local =nodejs_tools=
binary path to both Emacs' internal ~exec-path~ list and the ~$PATH~ environment
variable.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(with-eval-after-load 'exec-path-from-shell
  (let ((local-node-bin (expand-file-name "nodejs_tools/node_modules/.bin" user-emacs-directory)))
    (when (file-directory-p local-node-bin)
      (add-to-list 'exec-path local-node-bin)
      (setenv "PATH" (concat local-node-bin path-separator (getenv "PATH"))))))
#+end_src

** Platform Modifier Configuration
Prevent macOS system-level command key handling from overriding internal Emacs
keymap definitions when running under macOS port builds.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(when (boundp 'mac-pass-command-to-system)
  (setq mac-pass-command-to-system nil))
#+end_src

** WSLg Cursor Refresh
WSLg can occasionally fail to update the mouse cursor after a long-running
operation. Refresh the cursor after commands, but only for graphical Emacs
sessions running under WSL.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defun cfg-core/wsl-p ()
  "Return non-nil when running under WSL."
  (or (getenv "WSL_INTEROP")
      (and (file-readable-p "/proc/version")
           (with-temp-buffer
             (insert-file-contents "/proc/version")
             (goto-char (point-min))
             (re-search-forward "microsoft\\|WSL" nil t)))))

(defun cfg-core/wsl-refresh-cursor ()
  "Refresh the WSLg display."
  (when (and (eq system-type 'gnu/linux)
             (cfg-core/wsl-p)
             (display-graphic-p))
    (redisplay t)))

(when (and (eq system-type 'gnu/linux)
           (cfg-core/wsl-p)
           (display-graphic-p))
  (add-hook 'post-command-hook #'cfg-core/wsl-refresh-cursor))
#+end_src

** Restart Emacs from within Emacs
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(use-package restart-emacs)
#+end_src

** Try a new package without installing it
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(use-package try)
#+end_src

* Keybindings
Registers leader keybindings to toggle focus mode and olivetti on demand.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(cfg-keys/leader-def
  "C-M-r" '(restart-emacs :which-key "Restart Emacs"))
#+end_src

* System Setup
No system setup required.
